hed: Trump moves to ban Canadian alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles as Ottawa’s counter-tariffs take effect
dek: Canada’s counter-tariffs on roughly $20–28 billion of U.S. goods took effect at 12:01 a.m. ET Tuesday. Tuesday night President Trump signed proclamations to ban certain Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy products, and motorcycles and mopeds from importation effective Sept. 29; additional Canadian goods face up to 50% tariffs, and GSA/USTR were directed to remove Canadian products from federal procurement schedules. Prime Minister Mark Carney said a pivot “will come at a cost.” USTR Ambassador Jamieson Greer framed the bans as a response to Canada’s retaliation after talks stalled.
alt: Ambassador Bridge spanning the Detroit River between the United States and Canada
byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: BBC, ABC News, and NBC News frame Trump’s import bans on Canadian alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles as an escalation after Ottawa’s counter-tariffs took effect, with Carney warning of economic cost.

cr.body: CBS News, the Washington Examiner, and USTR’s Greer statement stress Section 338 proclamations, Sept. 29 effective dates, procurement removals, and reciprocity after Canada’s retaliation.

stack_blurb: Import bans effective Sept. 29; Canada counter-tariffs began Tuesday.
seo_description: Canada’s counter-tariffs began Tuesday; Trump proclamations ban certain Canadian alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles effective Sept. 29 and raise other tariffs.
